_source: ADR Chapter 3.3 — special provisions. PART 2 — numbers 291–364.

provisions.291: Radioactive material also meeting the criteria of other classes: (a) in excepted quantities — packaging per 3.5.2/3.5.3 plus the requirements of 1.7.1.5; (b) above those limits — classified according to the predominant subsidiary hazard, with the transport document name supplemented by 'Radioactive material, excepted package'; (c) Chapter 3.4 (LQ) does not apply to (b); (d) if exempted from the other classes — classified purely under Class 7 plus 1.7.1.5. Also covers design requirements for refrigerating machines containing flammable liquefied gas, exempted below 12 kg of gas.
provisions.293: Definitions of matches: storm (friction-sensitive mixture plus pyrotechnic composition), safety (ignite only on a prepared striking surface on the box), strike-anywhere (ignite on any hard surface), wax vesta matches.
provisions.295: Batteries need not be individually marked if the marking is shown on the pallet.
provisions.296: Life-saving appliances (life rafts, life jackets, escape slides) — UN 2990 (self-inflating) / UN 3072 (other); may contain limited dangerous goods (Class 1 signal devices, 1.4S cartridges up to 3.2 g, Class 2 group A/O gases, batteries, first-aid kits, matches); small kits ≤40 kg with gas in receptacles ≤120 ml are not subject to ADR.
provisions.300: Fish meal/fish waste/krill meal — loading prohibited when the temperature is >35°C or more than 5°C above ambient.
provisions.301: Applies only to devices/instruments containing dangerous goods as a residue or integral component (not to articles listed explicitly in Table A); quantity limited per the LQ values (column 7a); different goods must be segregated; directional arrows required for liquids needing them.
provisions.302: Fumigated transport units (containing no other dangerous goods) are subject only to the provisions of 5.5.2.
provisions.303: Receptacles must conform to the gas classification codes of 2.2.2.
provisions.304: Applies only to unactivated batteries containing dry potassium hydroxide, activated with water before use.
provisions.305: Materials at a concentration ≤50 mg/kg are not subject to ADR.
provisions.306: Applies only to substances too insensitive for Class 1 based on Test Series 2.
provisions.307: Applies only to ammonium nitrate based fertilizers meeting the classification procedure of Part III, Chapter 39; requires approval of the competent authority of the country of origin.
provisions.309: Non-sensitized emulsions/suspensions/gels (ANE) for the manufacture of type E explosives — specified composition (60-85% ammonium nitrate plus additives), compliance with Test Series 8 and competent authority approval.
provisions.310: Small production runs (≤100 units) or prototype cells/batteries for testing — exempted from part of 2.2.9.1.7.1; packed per P910/LP905; transport document must state 'Carriage in accordance with special provision 310'.
provisions.311: Substances only with the agreement of the competent authority (testing per Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part I); packaging must maintain the diluent level.
provisions.314: Substances prone to exothermic decomposition (initiated by heat or metallic contamination) — protect from sunlight/heat, provide good ventilation.
provisions.315: Not applicable to Class 6.1 substances meeting the inhalation toxicity criteria for packing group I.
provisions.316: Applies only to dry calcium hypochlorite in non-friable tablets.
provisions.317: 'Fissile-excepted' applies only to material/packages excepted in accordance with 2.2.7.2.3.5.
provisions.318: Name supplemented with the technical name; for unknown infectious substances suspected to be Category A, add 'Suspected Category A infectious substance' in brackets.
provisions.319: Substances packed per packing instruction P650 are not subject to any other provisions of ADR.
provisions.321: Storage systems are always considered to contain hydrogen.
provisions.322: Goods in non-friable tablet form fall under packing group III.
provisions.325: Non-fissile or fissile-excepted uranium hexafluoride is classified under UN 2978.
provisions.326: Fissile uranium hexafluoride is classified under UN 2977.
provisions.327: Waste aerosols/gas cartridges (consigned per 5.4.1.1.3.1) — UN 1950/2037 for repair or disposal; packed per P207+PP87, or P003+PP17/PP96, or LP200+L2; damaged ones in salvage packagings/pressure receptacles.
provisions.328: Fuel cell cartridges contained in, or packed with, equipment; design requirements (leak-tightness, pressure, 1.2 m drop test); lithium batteries within a fuel cell cartridge system are additionally subject to UN 3091/3481/3552.
provisions.332: Magnesium nitrate hexahydrate is not subject to ADR.
provisions.333: Ethanol/motor fuel or petrol blends for spark-ignition engines fall under this entry regardless of volatility.
provisions.334: A fuel cell cartridge may contain an activator with two independent means of preventing accidental mixing.
provisions.335: Mixtures of solids with environmentally hazardous substances (liquid/solid) — UN 3077 (no visible leakage) or UN 3082 (with leakage); small quantities (<10 ml/<10 g) absorbed without release are not subject to ADR.
provisions.336: Air transport: activity of LSA-II/III (non-flammable solid) ≤3000 A2.
provisions.337: Air transport: activity limits for Type B(U)/B(M) — depending on the material (3000 A1/100000 A2 for special form, 3000 A2 for others).
provisions.338: Fuel cell cartridges containing flammable liquefied gas: strength ≥2× the vapour pressure at 55°C, ≤200 ml of gas (≤1000 kPa at 55°C), hot water bath test.
provisions.339: Fuel cell cartridges containing hydrogen in metal hydride: water capacity ≤120 ml, pressure at 55°C ≤5 MPa; detailed design and testing requirements (drop, fire, cycling, leak-tightness) plus marking (pressure, serial number, expiry date).
provisions.340: Chemical/first aid/polyester resin kits in excepted quantities per Chapter 3.5; Class 5.2 substances without an individual EQ code may use code E2.
provisions.342: Glass ampoules/capsules containing ethylene oxide (≤30 ml per inner packaging, ≤300 ml per outer packaging) for sterilizers may be carried per Chapter 3.5 despite an E0 code, subject to leak-tightness testing and double containment.
provisions.343: Crude petroleum containing hydrogen sulfide at a concentration presenting an inhalation hazard — packing group assigned combining flammability and inhalation toxicity.
provisions.344: The requirements of 6.2.6 (for pressure receptacles) must be met.
provisions.345: Gas in an open cryogenic receptacle ≤1 l with vacuum insulation is not subject to ADR when placed in an outer packaging with cushioning/absorbent material.
provisions.346: Open cryogenic receptacle per P203, only for UN 1977 (nitrogen, refrigerated liquid, absorbed in a porous material), is not subject to any other provisions of ADR.
provisions.347: The entry applies only where Test Series 6(d) has shown no dangerous effect spreading beyond the package.
provisions.348: Lithium batteries (from 2012) and sodium-ion batteries (from 2026) must show the energy storage capacity (Wh) marked on the casing.
provisions.349: Mixtures of hypochlorite with an ammonium salt — carriage prohibited; UN 1791 hypochlorite solution is Class 8.
provisions.350: Ammonium bromate, ammonium chlorate, ammonium chlorite, ammonium permanganate and their solutions/mixtures with an ammonium salt — carriage prohibited.
provisions.356: Metal hydride storage systems (intended for installation in vehicles/machinery) require approval of the competent authority of the manufacturing country plus a document confirming that approval. Petroleum with an inhalation hazard from H2S is classified under UN 3494.
provisions.357: A solution of nitroglycerin in alcohol (1-5%) is Class 3/UN 3064 if it meets P300; otherwise Class 1/UN 0144.
provisions.360: Vehicles powered by lithium or sodium-ion batteries are assigned UN 3556/3557/3558; lithium batteries powering a transport unit externally are assigned UN 3536.
provisions.361: Electric double-layer capacitors >0.3 Wh: requirements (discharge/short-circuit protection, 95 kPa pressure resistance, venting, Wh marking); ≤0.3 Wh not subject to ADR; different exemption thresholds depending on Wh and mode of installation.
provisions.363: Engines/machinery powered by dangerous fuels (internal combustion or fuel cell) — when drained, not subject to ADR; with liquid Class 3 fuel → UN 3528; with flammable gas → UN 3529; environmentally hazardous → UN 3530; design requirements, valve marking, labels/placards according to fuel/tank volume thresholds (60 l/450 l/1000 l/3000 l).
provisions.364: Further detail on label/placard thresholds for UN 3528/3529/3530, and a requirement to state 'Carriage in accordance with special provision 363' in the transport document above 1000 l of fuel.
